Your transition into  your personal anecdote about teaching resonated. I was never formally a teacher nor even a tutor, as formal titles. I didn't necessarily do the intentional dress rehearsals and practices either. However, I often found myself in a role of instructor, tutor, exam preparation facilitator, team lead, etc. There was an expectation of expertise. At a minimum, there was an expectation of knowing how to obtain the correct answers and information when needed. Needing to know and understand a subject well enough to also explain it to someone else helped me to deliberately focus my personal learning in a way that was accidentally, "Active Learning," or, "Active Recall." I pictured a wall in front of the person or team that I was helping. It didn't matter if I could easily comprehend a subject. What mattered was getting that person past the wall that was keeping *THEM* from understanding the subject. Everything that I was learning also needed two or three different ways to better explain it to someone else that wasn't immediately understanding it. 
In college, and in various workplaces, I helped many people. Whenever I was working on a subject with someone else, those were the subjects that were the easiest to remember for reports, presentations, quizzes, and exams. I can best describe it as the act of intentionally looking at a matter from multiple viewpoints build up proverbial muscle memories that I could access years down the road when all else had been forgotten.

Ngl, I don't use shapes for the limbs, only for the pelvis, chest, and head. Most of the time, for the head I usually draw an oval, and if perspective-wise, I usually add a circle behind the oval to fit the brain. However, as you said, if the figure is soft or heavier in size, I use rounder shapes like ovals and circles. I never use triangles; I have never used triangles for anatomy or anything, to be honest. I only use triangles for the hand, and the base is rounded in a specific way that matches the placement of the fingers. I use ovals for the base and heel of the foot, as well as a slanted line for the toes. I learned how to draw hands from Draw Like a Sir (😍) and feet by looking at my own. For limbs, I use lines.
